4. Type in the title of your sub-section.

Alternatively, you can also use the keyboard shortcut "Ctrl + Shift + >" (or Command + Shift + > on a Mac) to create a new heading and then enter the text.

To uncompress a .docx file and view its XML data:

1. Rename the .docx file to a .zip file, since .docx files are actually just zipped archives containing XML files.
2. Right-click on the .zip file (now renamed) and select "Extract All" (or use your preferred unzip tool).
3. Open the extracted folder and navigate to the "word/" directory within it.
4. Inside the "word/" directory, you'll find a series of XML files, each representing different parts of the document's content, such as text, formatting, and styles.

Some common XML files you might find include:

* document.xml: The main document file containing the text content.
* styles.xml: Stores the document's style definitions, such as font sizes and paragraph spacing.
* settings.xml: Contains settings specific to the .docx file, like page layout and margins.

You can open these XML files in any text editor or use an XML viewer to inspect their contents. Keep in mind that these files are highly structured and contain a lot of technical information about the document's format and content.

Note that not all .docx files will have exactly the same structure, as different documents may use different features and settings. However, this process should give you a good starting point for exploring the XML data within your .docx file.
